content: The User contributions pages provide a detailed record of the edits made by a specific user. These pages are specific to individual projects, meaning that a contributions page for one project, such as Meta, will not display edits made to other projects like Wikipedia. Reviewing your contributions can help you recall which pages you have worked on and allow you to revisit them easily. Additionally, it enables you to check if any subsequent edits have been made to those pages. This functionality allows you to monitor pages even if they are not on your watchlist. Contributions pages for other users can also be accessed, which can be useful for understanding their editing activity or identifying problematic behavior, such as vandalism or copyright violations. To access your own contributions page, you can click on My contributions, which is typically located at the top of the page or on the left-hand side of the interface. To view another user's contributions, if the user has a registered account, you can navigate to their user page and click on User contributions. This option is available even if their user page has not been edited yet. If the user does not have a registered account, you can access their contributions by clicking on their IP address in the Recent Changes or Page History sections, or by entering their IP address into the search box and pressing Go. The user contributions page displays edits in reverse chronological order, with the most recent edits listed first. Each edit is presented on a single line, which includes the time and date of the edit, the name of the page edited, a summary of the edit, and other diagnostic details. The username or IP address of the contributor is displayed prominently. You can filter the results by selecting a specific namespace, such as Template, from a dropdown menu and pressing Go. The time and date of each edit are clearly indicated. The (hist) link allows you to view the full history of the page, which is useful for examining all edits made to that page, especially if you want to review changes made by others after your own edits. The (diff) link provides a comparison between the selected edit and the current version of the page, showing the changes made. The current version of the page is displayed below the changes for context. Minor edits, indicated by an m, represent small corrections or adjustments to a page. The name of the page where the edit occurred is displayed, but if the page has been renamed, the new name will be shown. The edit summary, which is the text entered by the user in the edit summary box, is also displayed. If the edit is the most recent revision of the page, it is marked with (top), indicating that the page remains as the user last saved it. This can help you monitor pages, as the absence of (top) on your last edit indicates that the page has been modified since your contribution. For administrators (sysops), a rollback link is available for reverting edits. If an edit is made to a specific section of a page, the edit summary will begin with an arrow link and grey text, which automatically identifies the section edited. The black text in the summary is the standard edit summary provided by the user. For users with a small number of edits, all contributions may fit on a single page. However, if the edits span multiple pages, navigation links will appear, allowing you to view the user's most recent edits (Latest), oldest edits (Earliest), or the next or previous set of edits (Next n / Previous n). The number of edits displayed per page can be adjusted to 20, 50, 100, 250, or 500. Increasing the number of edits per page reduces the total number of pages but lengthens each page. The selected number replaces n in the navigation links (e.g., Next 100 / Previous 100). The creation of new pages is also shown on the contributions page. However, certain actions are not displayed, such as edits to pages that have been deleted (unless restored), uploading a new image that replaces an existing one with the same name, or the deletion or restoration of a page (if performed by a sysop). The URL for a user contributions page typically follows this format: `Contributions&target=XX` or `Contributions/XX`, where XX represents the username or IP address. To view contributions on a specific subsite, such as Meta or Wikipedia, you need to adjust the subsite in the URL (e.g., `www.wikipedia.org` or `meta.wikimedia.org`). A shorter URL format, such as `Special:Contributions/XX`, can also be used to link to a user contributions page. Interwiki links function as usual (e.g., `w:Special:Contributions/XX`). To view edits from a single namespace, you can use the long-form URL and specify the namespace number (e.g., `Contributions&target=XX&namespace=4`). It is important to note that your contributions are publicly visible and can be accessed by anyone. Therefore, you should remain mindful of this when making edits.
